llm.summary: This skill is broadly about setting up OpenClaw agents, but its scripts have unsafe input handling, persistent credential/config changes, and automatic cross-agent permissions that need review before use.

dimensions.detail: The scripts write under the OpenClaw state directory, modify openclaw.json, store messaging credentials, back up config, and restart the gateway; unvalidated manifest paths and agent IDs can escape intended boundaries.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package contains local helper scripts and no observed remote payload retrieval or install hook, but those scripts perform mutating setup actions when invoked.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Manifest-provided name, role, and emoji values are written directly into persistent startup files such as SOUL.md and IDENTITY.md without validation or a user review step.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Persistent workspaces, config entries, credentials, bindings, and agent-to-agent allow-list changes are expected for the purpose, but they are broad and lack clear opt-in controls for cross-agent access.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose of creating agents and channel bindings is coherent, but the documentation overstates channel support and batch mode silently adds every created agent to agentToAgent.allow.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review and harden the scripts before installing or running this skill. Only use manifests you authored and inspected, avoid putting live tokens in chat or version-controlled JSON files, validate agent IDs as simple slugs, remove automatic agentToAgent.allow changes unless explicitly needed, and expect the batch script to modify OpenClaw config and restart the gateway.
llm.findings:
[TP4] unexpected: Verified a real description mismatch: documentation lists WhatsApp, Signal, and Google Chat broadly, while batch code only handles Telegram, Feishu, Discord, and Slack; single-agent setup also leaves channel binding manual.
[SQP-2] expected: Credential collection is purpose-aligned for messaging channels, but the README and examples encourage tokens/secrets in prompts, manifests, and config without adequate handling warnings.
[LP3] expected: Shell execution and config edits are expected for agent setup, but the skill does not define a narrow permission boundary or confirmation model for writes and restarts.
[RA2] expected: Downgraded as unauthorized system persistence: I found workspace/config persistence and backups, but no cron job, startup service, or backdoor-style persistence.
[SQP-3] expected: The hardcoded Chinese generated agent text is verified, but this is mainly a disclosure/usability issue rather than a standalone security concern.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Verified batch mode automatically grants every created agent agent-to-agent authorization, which is broader than required for channel setup.
[T09] unexpected: Verified unsafe interpolation of the manifest path into python3 -c source, allowing crafted filenames to execute unintended Python code as the invoking user.
[T05] unexpected: Verified unvalidated agent IDs and names are used as filesystem path components, allowing traversal or absolute-path writes to predetermined Markdown filenames.
[T02] unexpected: Verified manifest metadata is embedded into persistent agent startup context without sanitization, allowing a malicious manifest to poison later agent behavior.
